data.narrative:
Radiant, a Series D nuclear energy company founded by Doug Bernauer, has raised $465M+ to date. The relevant peer universe consists of 10 comparable companies across nuclear energy—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private entities including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy—though narrow-stage and valuation-tier filtering yielded insufficient datapoints for robust peer median analysis.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach, given constraints on peer comparables. Using Radiant's last post-money valuation of $1.0B as the base and applying a typical 1.5x step-up multiplier for Series D progression yields an implied valuation of $1.5B. This represents the median of the triangulated range.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B to $1.7B, with $1.5B as the central estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient same-stage and similarly-scaled private nuclear energy comparables, which limits cross-validation through peer multiples. Valuation sensitivity to near-term technical milestones, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital efficiency relative to the peer set remains material. A tighter range would require either stage-adjacent peer data or evidence of material company-specific developments since the last funding event.
